name: Velocity Mapping
summary: Decides how your aiming curve and thumbstick aim map onto the game's maximum turn speed.

where.text: Edit your Config (pencil icon), then press the "..." under Aiming Sources and choose a Velocity Mapping.

citations.quote: To edit the current Config, press the pencil icon.
To access, press the "..." under Aiming Sources:
You can choose from the following Velocity Mappings:

definition.text: Velocity Mapping is a feature that allows you to further craft your aiming experience. It focuses on how your custom aiming curves and thumbstick aim maps to reticle velocity since both have a constrained range.

citations.quote: Velocity Mapping is a feature that allows you to further craft your aiming experience. It focuses on how your custom aiming curves and thumbstick aim maps to reticle velocity since both have a constrained range.

plainWords.text: On controller output, every console shooter has a maximum turn speed it can't exceed. That maximum differs by aiming angle.

citations.quote: All controller console shooters are limited by a maximum turn speed that the game cannot exceed. This maximum turn speed limit actually differs depending on aiming angle.

plainWords.text: The controller-output options: Standard maps your top speed to the game's maximum for each aiming angle. Uniform maps it to the game's supported maximum, so horizontal and vertical feel the same. Limit is Uniform with a top speed you choose. Reduce starts like Standard, then your top speed is "reduced by the specified velocity which cannot be exceeded" (XIM's wording).

citations.quote: Standard: Maximum velocity is mapped to the maximum reticle velocity of the game for that aiming angle.
Uniform: Maximum velocity is mapped to the maximum reticle velocity supported by the game resulting in a uniform horizontal and vertical aiming experience.
Limit: Same as Uniform, but, you can specify the maximum velocity that cannot be exceeded.
Reduce: Maximum velocity is mapped to the maximum reticle velocity of the game for that aiming angle and then reduced by the specified velocity which cannot be exceeded.

plainWords.text: For thumbstick aim, it only applies with Custom Stick Behavior.

citations.quote: For thumbstick aim, velocity mapping only applies when using custom stick behavior.

plainWords.text: Mouse output has different options. Primer covers controller output only, so they are left out here.

citations.quote: This customization differs depending if you are outputting as mouse or controller.
Do not use velocity mapping (default is Standard).

guidance.text: After changing it, your MATRIX may flash red (maximum turn speed reached) more often, if that light notification is on. You can't exceed the game's turn speed limit either way.

citations.quote: When customizing Velocity Mapping, your XIM MATRIX may notify that you've exceeded maximum turn speed more often. This is because no matter what, you cannot exceed the turn speed restrictions built into the game.

If you are gaming with controller output, then, you need to be aware of the game's maximum turn speed limit. All console shooters have different limits and your XIM MATRIX will notify you when you hit that limit by quickly flashing red so you can adjust accordingly.
Disabling light aim speed and mode light notifications

guidance.text: Only if you use Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB): don't use velocity mapping (leave it at Standard).

citations.quote: Do not use velocity mapping (default is Standard).

guidance.caveat: Applies only when Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB) is on. SAB is a controller-output feature for games with extra input requirements.

aimStyles.text: Not only snaps and big turns. For custom aiming curves, and for thumbstick aim with Custom Stick Behavior, Velocity Mapping sets the reticle velocity your maximum maps to. A curve runs from 0 to 100% of that velocity, so changing the mapping can change slower movements too. In XIM's example illustration, Standard gives each aiming angle its own maximum and Uniform gives every angle the same one.

citations.quote: Velocity Mapping is a feature that allows you to further craft your aiming experience. It focuses on how your custom aiming curves and thumbstick aim maps to reticle velocity since both have a constrained range.
A curve represents how your reticle speed transitions from 0 to 100% velocity (bottom left of the curve to upper right).
Standard: Maximum velocity is mapped to the maximum reticle velocity of the game for that aiming angle.

For thumbstick aim, velocity mapping only applies when using custom stick behavior.

aimStyles.reasoning: A curve 'represents how your reticle speed transitions from 0 to 100% velocity', and Velocity Mapping sets which reticle velocity your maximum maps to, so every point on the curve scales with it, not just the top. XIM's illustration (Aim-Settings-018.png, 'RETICLE VELOCITY RANGE') draws each Standard curve from 0 °/s to a different maximum (85 °/s up, 215 °/s diagonal, 300 °/s sideways) and the Uniform curve to 300 °/s at every angle. Those are example values for 'a particular game', not Destiny 2. No source ties Velocity Mapping to one aim style.

aimStyles.text: Uniform maps your maximum velocity to the same reticle speed in every direction, for what XIM calls "a uniform horizontal and vertical aiming experience". It does not remove the game's limits. The game's maximum turn speed still differs by aiming angle, so fast moves in a direction with a lower limit (vertical, in XIM's example) are still capped by the game. Your MATRIX may also notify you that you've hit maximum turn speed more often.

citations.quote: All controller console shooters are limited by a maximum turn speed that the game cannot exceed. This maximum turn speed limit actually differs depending on aiming angle.
Standard: Maximum velocity is mapped to the maximum reticle velocity of the game for that aiming angle.
Uniform: Maximum velocity is mapped to the maximum reticle velocity supported by the game resulting in a uniform horizontal and vertical aiming experience.

When customizing Velocity Mapping, your XIM MATRIX may notify that you've exceeded maximum turn speed more often. This is because no matter what, you cannot exceed the turn speed restrictions built into the game.

aimStyles.reasoning: In XIM's example illustration, Uniform maps every direction to 300 °/s, where Standard maps vertical to 85 °/s. The game's limit "differs depending on aiming angle", and "no matter what, you cannot exceed the turn speed restrictions built into the game". XIM adds that after customizing Velocity Mapping your MATRIX "may notify that you've exceeded maximum turn speed more often". XIM's numbers are an example "for a particular game", not Destiny 2's limits.

confusions.name: Velocity Calibration
confusions.note: Teaches the MATRIX how fast the reticle moves in your game. It is required for mouse output; for controller output it is an advanced option that XIM discourages. Velocity Mapping sets the reticle velocity that the maximum of your aiming curves and thumbstick aim maps to.

confusions.name: Standard (smoothing)
confusions.note: The speed-adaptive smoothing mode. Unrelated to the Standard velocity mapping.

confusions.name: Standard (Game Settings sync)
confusions.note: A sync method for in-game settings. Unrelated to the Standard velocity mapping.

confusions.name: Limit (Advanced SAB)
confusions.note: An Advanced SAB value that "Restricts how fast the stick can move". Not the Limit velocity mapping.
